tool_input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
test(daemon): add gate-4 negative control and combined end-to-end test

TestBuildStageContract_RealEthosCLIRejectsMalformedContract: gate 4's
negative control. The existing test only asserted success; this
deletes evaluator.handle from an otherwise-valid generated contract and
asserts the real ethos CLI rejects it, so a systemic harness failure
(broken isolation, PATH misconfiguration, a swallowed error) can no
longer make every `ethos mission create` call spuriously succeed
unnoticed. Manually verified this control can fail: restored contract
validity, ran it, observed FAIL, reverted.

TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd (internal/daemon/harness_test.go): drives gates
1 and 2 (both directions) plus gates 3 and 4's positive case together
through the real OnNewMail entry point, bypassing Poller entirely
(first-poll suppression + 1m minimum interval make it unusable for a
pre-commit gate; OnNewMail + Stop() is the deterministic sync point).
Only daemon.Spawner is faked. This file is `package daemon_test`
(external), not the white-box convention every other file in this
directory uses, because its daemontest import would otherwise close
the same import cycle daemontest's own package comment documents.

Also converts TestBuildStageContract_ValidatesAgainstRealEthosCLI's
t.Skip to t.Fatalf naming the install remedy, and switches it to
testenv.IsolateEthos -- no t.Skip survives anywhere in this tier.

Manually verified (then reverted) that gates 1, 2, 3, and 4's negative
cases all genuinely fail when their guards are disabled -- none of
these assertions is tautological.
EOF
)"
